title: Local decomposition map lands in geometric and Weil subgroups
statement: Let $C_0/k_0$ be a curve in the sense of [d-real-setup], let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a nonempty open with finite complement $S_0$, and let $s\in S_0$. Put $k_s=\kappa(s)$, $U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$, and $K_s=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal O_{C_0,s}^{h})$, where henselization is as in [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Choose an algebraic closure $\overline K_s$ and a compatible algebraic closure $\overline{k_s}$ of the residue field. Write $D_s=\operatorname{Gal}(\overline K_s/K_s)$ and $G_s=\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{k_s}/k_s)$ as in [def-real-boundary-absolute-galois-group], let $r_s:D_s\to G_s$ be the residue homomorphism of [lem-real-henselian-residue-galois-action], put $I_s=\ker(r_s)$, and let $W(K_s)=r_s^{-1}(\langle\Phi_s\rangle)$, where $\Phi_s$ is geometric Frobenius of $k_s$. Choose the geometric point $\bar\eta_s$ over $\operatorname{Spec}K_s\to U_0$, a base point $\bar u$ on $U$, and a path $\gamma:F_{\bar\eta_s}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\bar u}$ as in [def-real-boundary-decomposition-path]. For a finite etale cover $P$ of $U_0$, an element $z\in|P_{\bar\eta_s}|$ is a $U_0$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\overline K_s\to P$, and $\sigma\in D_s$ acts on the local geometric fibre by $a_{\sigma,P}(z)=z\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$. With $\pi_1(U_0,\bar u)$ and $\pi_1(U,\bar u)$ the fundamental groups of [def-galois-fibre-functor], the latter viewed in the former through $U\to U_0$, the formula $\theta_s(\sigma)_P=\gamma_P\circ a_{\sigma,P}\circ\gamma_P^{-1}$, equivalently path transport of the map induced by $\operatorname{Spec}K_s\to U_0$ through [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality], defines a continuous homomorphism $\theta_s:D_s\to\pi_1(U_0,\bar u)$. It satisfies $\theta_s(I_s)\subseteq\pi_1(U,\bar u)$ and $\theta_s(W(K_s))\subseteq W(U_0,\bar u)$, with Weil group as in [def-wf-weil-group].

proof.text: The projection $C=C_0\times_{k_0}k\to C_0$ is surjective by surjectivity for a field extension and its preservation under base change. Thus $C$ is nonempty, since $C_0$ is; $C$ is connected by [d-real-setup], and its continuous surjective image $C_0$ is connected too. On affine charts, the characterization of smooth scheme morphisms by smooth ring maps and the smooth-ring base-change theorem show that $C$ is smooth over $k$. Finite type of $C$ follows directly by tensoring the finitely many generators of each chart in a finite affine cover of $C_0$. Both $C_0$ and $C$ are Noetherian by the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem, since the spectra of fields are Noetherian. Smooth algebras over a field have regular local rings, so both schemes are regular. The regular-Noetherian-connected irreducibility statement therefore makes $C_0$ and $C$ irreducible. This uses no dimension invariance under field extension.

source.place: the decomposition homomorphism clause, expanded using finite-cover fibre functors and equivariant reduction

proof.text: The open $U\subset C$ contains the chosen point $\bar u$, so it is nonempty. A nonempty open of an irreducible space is irreducible: any two nonempty relatively open subsets are nonempty opens of the ambient irreducible space and intersect. Thus $U$ is connected, and $U_0$ is geometrically connected. The open $U_0$ is quasi-compact because $C_0$ is Noetherian, and locally of finite type over $k_0$ by its affine charts; hence it is of finite type. It is separated because its diagonal is the restriction of the separated diagonal of $C_0$. These verify the Weil-group hypotheses. Since $C_0$ is irreducible of dimension one, every nongeneric point is closed: a further proper specialization would give a chain of length two after adjoining the generic point. The proper closed complement $S_0$ omits the generic point, so $s$ is closed. Applying the closed-point field theorem to $C_0/k_0$ gives $e_s=[k_s:k_0]\geq1$ finite, and therefore $|k_s|=q^{e_s}$.

source.place: the decomposition homomorphism clause, expanded using finite-cover fibre functors and equivariant reduction

proof.text: For every cover $P\to U_0$, precomposition with $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$ preserves the fibre, since $\sigma$ fixes $K_s$. For a morphism of covers $h:P\to Q$, associativity gives $h\circ a_{\sigma,P}(z)=a_{\sigma,Q}(h\circ z)$. Also $\operatorname{Spec}(\tau)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma\tau)$, so $a_{\sigma,P}a_{\tau,P}=a_{\sigma\tau,P}$, with identity $a_1$ and inverse $a_{\sigma^{-1}}$. Hence $a_\sigma$ is a natural automorphism of the local fibre functor. Conjugating its components by the natural bijections $\gamma_P$ gives a natural automorphism of $F_{\bar u}$ and preserves products and identity. This is precisely an element $\theta_s(\sigma)\in\pi_1(U_0,\bar u)$.

source.place: the decomposition homomorphism clause, expanded using finite-cover fibre functors and equivariant reduction

proof.text: The homomorphism is continuous in the Krull topology. A point of the finite geometric fibre of $P$ is given by a homomorphism from the finite etale $K_s$-algebra of $P\times_{U_0}\operatorname{Spec}K_s$ to $\overline K_s$. Choose finitely many algebra generators; their images are algebraic over $K_s$. The subgroup fixing these finitely many elements is open by definition of the Krull topology and fixes that point. Since the fibre is finite, the kernel of its permutation action is a finite intersection of such open stabilizers. Thus each component $\sigma\mapsto a_{\sigma,P}$ is continuous. Conjugation by the fixed finite permutation $\gamma_P$ preserves continuity, so the product-induced topology in the definition of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar u})$ proves continuity of $\theta_s$. Pullback of a cover along $\operatorname{Spec}K_s\to U_0$ identifies its local fibre by projection. The characterization of $f_*$ in [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality] therefore gives exactly the same permutations; subsequent conjugation by $\gamma$ gives the displayed formula. This also proves the claimed agreement with the functorial map.

source.place: the decomposition homomorphism clause, expanded using finite-cover fibre functors and equivariant reduction

proof.text: Apply equivariant reduction to $R=\mathcal O_{C_0,s}^h$, $K=K_s$ and $\Omega=\overline K_s$. The henselization $H$ is henselian local by definition. To check its residue field, put $A=\mathcal O_{C_0,s}$. The field $k_s=A/\mathfrak m_A$ is henselian: its maximal ideal is zero, so idempotent lifting modulo that ideal is the identity. The universal property of $H$ applied to the local residue map $A\to k_s$ gives a local map $H\to k_s$ extending it. On residue fields the composite $k_s\to\kappa(H)\to k_s$ is the identity. The second arrow is an injective field homomorphism, and its image contains $k_s$, so these are inverse isomorphisms. Thus $\kappa(H)=k_s$ under the structural identification. Let $k'\subset\overline K_s$ be the elements algebraic over $k_0$. Reduction gives $t:k'\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline{k_s}$ and the equality $\sigma|_{k'}=t^{-1}r_s(\sigma)t$. On a constant cover $P_L=U_0\times_{k_0}\operatorname{Spec}L$, with $L/k_0$ finite, the local fibre is the set of $k_0$-embeddings $L\to\overline K_s$, all landing in $k'$, and $a_\sigma$ is postcomposition by $\sigma|_{k'}$. Thus this displayed equality computes the local action on every finite constant cover directly. No identification of the chosen path with a path over $k_0$ is imposed.

source.place: the decomposition homomorphism clause, expanded using finite-cover fibre functors and equivariant reduction

proof.text: If $\sigma\in I_s$, the equality in step 5 says that $\sigma|_{k'}=1$. If $\sigma\in W(K_s)$, write $r_s(\sigma)=\Phi_s^n$ for $n\in\mathbf Z$ and put $m=e_sn$. With $\Phi'_0=(x\mapsto x^q)^{-1}$ on $k'$, the definition of geometric Frobenius gives $t^{-1}\Phi_s t=(\Phi'_0)^{e_s}$, since $|k_s|=q^{e_s}$. Hence $\sigma|_{k'}=(\Phi'_0)^m$. For each finite extension $L/k_0$, let $b_{m,L}$ be the cover automorphism $\operatorname{id}_{U_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}((x\mapsto x^q)^{-m}|_L)$ of $P_L$. If a local fibre point corresponds to $\lambda:L\to k'$, its image under $a_\sigma$ is $(\Phi'_0)^m\lambda=\lambda(x\mapsto x^q)^{-m}|_L$, the image under $b_{m,L}$. Naturality of $\gamma$ for the morphism $b_{m,L}$ therefore transports this to the same deck transformation on the fibre at $\bar u$. At $\bar u$ it is the permutation induced by $\Phi_0^m$, where $\Phi_0=(x\mapsto x^q)^{-1}$ on the fixed $k$. Since the arithmetic projection $h:\pi_1(U_0,\bar u)\to\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$ is defined on these constant covers, we obtain $h(\theta_s(\sigma))=\Phi_0^{e_sn}$. For inertia the identical argument uses $b_{0,L}=1$ and gives $h(\theta_s(\sigma))=1$. All formulas hold for negative $n$ as well, using inverse field automorphisms.

source.place: the decomposition homomorphism clause, expanded using finite-cover fibre functors and equivariant reduction

proof.text: For $\sigma\in W(K_s)$, the equality just proved puts $h(\theta_s(\sigma))$ in $\langle\Phi_0\rangle$, so the inverse-image definition of the Weil group gives $\theta_s(\sigma)\in W(U_0,\bar u)$, of degree $e_sn$. In particular if $\sigma\in I_s$, its image has trivial arithmetic projection, belongs to the Weil group, and has degree zero. The exact Weil degree sequence identifies its degree-zero kernel with the image of $\pi_1(U,\bar u)$. Therefore $\theta_s(I_s)\subseteq\pi_1(U,\bar u)$, and $\theta_s(W(K_s))\subseteq W(U_0,\bar u)$ as asserted.

One statement-only algebra comparison node isolates equivariant reduction of algebraic constants; it has no curves or Weil group. Existing curve, closed-point and Weil exact-sequence nodes are reused. Statement unchanged except naming the residue-map construction. Project and Mathlib searches found no complete attachment or leaf.
split_report.blueprint: d-real-boundary: the chosen geometric point/path and decomposition-group homomorphism carrying I_s into pi_1(U) and W(K_s) into W(U_0). No change to the unit route; later boundary-stalk and path-independence clauses are outside this item.

tool_uses.why: Zariski lemma gives finite boundary residue fields, a generic finite-type tool.
Generic finite-cover functoriality characterizes the decomposition map prescribed by the unit.
The kernel of the Weil degree is the geometric fundamental group; the unit uses this standard Weil group structure.
Surjectivity of the base-field extension projection is a generic scheme tool used to descend connectedness.
Base change of the surjective map of field spectra gives C to C_0 surjective.
The base change of affine smooth coordinate rings is smooth, verifying the geometric setup.
Finite-type schemes over fields are Noetherian, used only to verify curve and open hypotheses.
Smooth affine coordinate rings over either ground field have regular stalks.
Regular Noetherian nonempty connected schemes are irreducible; this avoids using an algebraically-closed curve theorem before checking its dimension hypotheses.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NV-9666d0648 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, the new node, every cited statement, the unit record and blueprint d-real-boundary.md (main-20261015), and Stacks Tags 04GH/00GN in algebra.tex; the review is in review.md. Steps 1-2: the base change C is nonempty, connected, smooth, Noetherian and regular, hence irreducible by rem-pc-regular-normal(3). U_0 is a valid Weil-group base (separated, finite type, geometrically connected), s is closed (the dimension-one chain argument holds) and kappa(s) is finite by lem-kun-closed-point-field(a). Step 3: the action is a left action (Spec(tau)Spec(sigma)=Spec(sigma tau)) and natural in the cover. Step 4: Krull continuity holds through generator stabilisers on finite fibres, and the formula agrees with f_* by the tau_P characterisation. Step 5: kappa(H)=k_s follows from the universal property, since the injective map back to k_s splits the inclusion. Step 6: the sign check goes through: postcomposition on constant-cover fibres matches how r is characterised in lem-wf-arithmetic-lift-fibre-path, and the deck map b_{m,L} sends lambda to lambda composed with phi^{-m}, which equals phi^{-m} composed with lambda. So h(theta(sigma))=Phi_0^{e_s n}, also for n<0. Step 7: the inverse-image definition gives landing in W(U_0), and inertia has degree 0, so lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence puts it in pi_1(U). New node lem-real-henselian-residue-galois-action is true as stated. It is checked on the cases kernel=m (B is the algebraic closure of the residue field, n=0), R=K finite, and non-reduced R; finiteness of the residue field is necessary and present. It has the correct B1-B9 form and three kinds of search, it is not a clause of the item, and grep of the DAG found no duplicate. Batch-5 check: lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence is a group-theoretic exact sequence whose proof cites only three definitions. Its link to sec-poincare-duality runs only through the definition def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves, which the item already reaches through def-wf-weil-group; the computed closure gains only that node itself. It is therefore outside both assumed statements. I accept all nine declared tool_uses. One inherited observation, not this delivery's fault: the statement presupposes, as the blueprint and d-real-boundary do, that Spec K_s -> C_0 factors through U_0 and that the henselization is a domain. This is true but no node states it; the maintainer should add one. No fix files.
